facts: Q1 2026 total revenues were $410.5 million, down 3% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $28.1 million, both below internal expectations due to harsh winter weather, a delayed construction season, Q4 2025 equipment sales pull-forward from tax legislation, and elevated self-insured health plan costs (~$3 million variance).

Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was reduced by $5 million on each end to a new range of $167.5 million to $182.5 million, with free cash flow before rent-to-sell decisioning expected at $100–$110 million, both back-half weighted.

Material Handling segment revenue fell ~4.7% year-over-year to $150.5 million, but bookings in the company's markets increased over 20% in the quarter, with March marking the strongest single booking month since June 2023.

Construction Equipment segment revenue was essentially flat year-over-year at $244.3 million, with April adding an incremental $25 million of rental fleet on rent versus March as the construction season opened.

New and used equipment gross margins increased 240 basis points quarter-over-quarter, supported by reduced dealer inventories, less OEM discounting, and stabilizing pricing (wholesale construction equipment PPI up ~5% in Q1).

Rental fleet gross book value was reduced by approximately $59.5 million year-over-year to $524.6 million, with management targeting sub-$500 million by year-end and another ~$30 million of disposals planned after $30 million completed in Q1.

Operating cash flow was $20.8 million, an improvement of $38.3 million versus Q1 2025, allowing net leverage to stay roughly flat versus year-end and maintaining liquidity of approximately $250 million, with a path to below 4.5x leverage by year-end.
Interest expense declined $2.4 million year-over-year to $19.5 million, reflecting deleveraging actions taken in 2025.

Ecoverse Master Distribution segment generated $17.1 million in revenue with tariff-related margin compression expected to end after Q1, supported by renegotiated OEM pricing and recent Supreme Court tariff ruling/IPA relief.

EBITDA built sequentially through the quarter with March adjusted EBITDA approximately 3x January's level, and management targets rental dollar utilization in the mid- to high 30s versus current levels.
Q3 2025 revenue was $11.5 million, down from $11.7 million in Q2 2025.
Cash position decreased to $10.3 million from $10.5 million at the end of Q2 2025.
The company expects both revenue and adjusted EBITDA to be sequentially lower in Q4 2025 compared to Q3 2025.
Management anticipates revenue growth on a run rate basis in the 10% range from year-end levels in 2026.
The company expects adjusted EBITDA margins of 10% or more in the course of 2026.
Marchex entered an agreement in principle to acquire Archenia for a $10 million convertible promissory note plus an earn-out of up to 4 million shares over 2 years.
The combined company with Archenia would have revenue run rates of approximately $15 million quarterly or approximately $60 million annualized.
Management believes the combined company's revenue could grow in the 15% to 20% range in 2026.
The company migrated more than 1,000 customers onto its new technology platform, with completion expected by year-end 2025.
Q3 2025 sales bookings accelerated to the highest levels of the year, with management expecting this momentum to continue and compound into 2026.
Sales of $374 million in Q3 2025 decreased approximately 6% versus the prior year, with sales volume accounting for about half of the change.
Adjusted EBITDA was $25 million, down $28 million from last year, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.6%.
The Chesterfield plant electrical outage and subsequent fire is expected to impact Q4 EBITDA by $7 million to $9 million primarily from unabsorbed fixed costs.
2025 CapEx is now expected to be $120 million to $125 million, reflecting $30 million full year cash conservation through refined risk-based prioritization.
The sustained growth program, which unlocks 200,000 tons of granular ammonium sulfate, is tracking roughly 15% below its capital budget.
Granular ammonium sulfate volume was up 20% year-over-year in Q3 2025.
Utilization across the integrated value chain was down roughly 4 percentage points sequentially from Q2 to Q3.
The company anticipates its cash tax rate being below 10% over the next few years, supported by 45Q carbon capture tax credits and 100% bonus depreciation.
The company expects a cumulative benefit of $100 million to $120 million from 45Q carbon capture tax credits across the life of the program.
Nearly 90% of the company's sales are in the U.S., largely insulating it from first-order impacts of reciprocal tariffs.
Q3 FY2026 net sales reached $1.2 billion, up 2% (~$19 million) year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $5.31, a 4% increase versus the prior year.

Acuity Brands Lighting (ABL) sales declined 2% to $905 million against a tough prior-year comparison (pre-tariff order pull-forward), and adjusted operating margin contracted 60 bps to 18.2%, though gross margin remained strong at 46.1%.
Acuity Intelligence Spaces (AIS) sales grew 15% to $304 million with adjusted operating profit up 22.5% to $76 million and operating margin expanding 150 bps to 25.1%, driven by Distech and QSC.
Management said lighting demand is 'firming' after softness from October through January, and Q4 should show sequential growth from Q3, though likely less steep than the Q3 step-up.
On a 2-year stacked basis, total ABL grew 1% and the combined independent/direct sales networks grew 4%, normalizing for tariff-driven order timing.
Year-to-date operating cash flow reached $520 million, $121 million higher than the prior-year period, supporting aggressive capital returns.
The company repaid $200 million of term loan, raised the dividend 18%, and repurchased over 766,000 shares for $230 million YTD, including ~500,000 shares this quarter at an average price of $281.
Acuity refinanced into a new 5-year $800 million unsecured revolving credit facility, upsizing capacity and extending maturities.
Distech is expanding into the data center vertical via the new Eclipse Resilience PLC controller, complementing its DDC platform and positioning the company to supply multiple hyperscalers.

Management flagged inflation pressures (metals, ~12% medical cost increase, memory chip supply shocks primarily affecting AIS) but expects continued ABL gross margin expansion through product vitality, productivity, and pricing even in a soft volume environment.
Air Products delivered fiscal year 2025 earnings per share of $12.03, above the midpoint of full year guidance, with operating income margin of 23.7% and return on capital of 10.1%.
The company returned $1.6 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2025, marking its 43rd consecutive year of dividend increases.
For fiscal year 2026, Air Products expects earnings per share in the range of $12.85 to $13.15, representing 7% to 9% growth from the prior year.
Since 2022, the company has identified 3,600 headcount reductions (16% of peak workforce), expected to contribute approximately $250 million in annual cost savings or $0.90 per share once complete.
Capital expenditures are expected to be approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026, declining to roughly $2.5 billion per year after large projects are completed.
The NEOM project is approximately 90% complete, with solar and wind power generation expected by early 2026 and full ammonia production availability in 2027.
Air Products has approximately $2.5 billion remaining to spend on underperforming projects from 2026 to 2028, which are not expected to contribute materially to operating income.

The company is evaluating proposals to divest carbon sequestration and ammonia production assets from its Louisiana blue hydrogen project and has halted new commitments until an offtake agreement is reached.
Helium headwinds are expected to continue in fiscal 2026 at approximately 4%, comparable to fiscal 2025 levels.
The company expects to be modestly cash flow positive in fiscal 2026 and is committed to staying cash flow neutral through 2028 as it closes out several projects.
Q1 2026 revenue was $80 million on 263 transactions, within the guided range of $70-95 million and 250-300 transactions.
Q2 2026 guidance calls for 300-350 transactions (14%-33% sequential growth), revenue of $80-90 million, and a narrower adjusted EBITDA loss than Q1.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $6.7 million in Q1 2026, with management targeting positive adjusted EBITDA before year-end 2026 at roughly 1,000 transactions per quarter.
Gross margin improved to 6.9% in Q1 2026 ($5.6 million gross profit) versus 6.5% in Q1 2025.
Operating expenses excluding property selling costs fell to $12.2 million, down from $16.7 million in Q1 2025, with over $140 million in annualized expenses removed since 2022.
Total liquidity exceeded $60 million at quarter end, including $41 million of unrestricted cash, and management does not anticipate needing incremental equity capital to execute the 2026 plan.
Aged inventory was reduced to fewer than 30 homes, down from fewer than 60 at the end of Q4 2025, aided by mortgage rate buydown incentives.
SCOUT AI deployment drove a 200+ basis point improvement in home contracting rates from January through March and contributed to a 37% year-over-year decline in cost per qualified lead.
Offerpad Renovate generated $5.7 million in Q1 2026 revenue (vs. $5.3 million in Q1 2025) at 20%-30% margins with no balance sheet capital required.

Cash Offer Marketplace grew over 60% year-over-year in 2025 and is expected to become a meaningful contributor to gross profit in the second half of 2026, while one-third of Cash Offer requests now come through the agent partnership program.
Q3 2025 organic revenue grew 4% year-over-year to $5.1 billion, with organic orders growth of 6% and book-to-bill at 1.06x.
Adjusted EPS was $1.07 per share, down 6% year-over-year, but would have been up high single digits excluding the approximately $0.16 of tariff impact.
The company raised the lower end of its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $4.51 to $4.63 per share, with tariffs expected to impact adjusted EPS by approximately $0.45 for the year.
Backlog exited the quarter at a record $21.2 billion, and the company secured multiple large system deals totaling nearly $0.5 billion in future revenue.

Pharmaceutical Diagnostics segment delivered 10% organic revenue growth and 14% EBIT growth, while Patient Care Solutions organic revenue declined 7% primarily due to a product hold that has now been resolved.
Advanced Visualization Solutions achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of year-over-year sales and margin growth, with organic revenue up 6% and segment EBIT margin up 180 basis points.
The company mitigated approximately 50% of its 2025 gross tariff exposure and expects a lower net tariff impact in 2026 versus 2025, making tariffs a tailwind to earnings growth next year.

Flyrcado will fall short of the $30 million 2025 target due to a deliberate decision to prioritize customer experience, but the company remains confident in its medium-term expectation of $500 million by 2028.
Free cash flow was $483 million in Q3 with 99% conversion, and the company repurchased approximately $100 million of shares during the quarter.
The company increased its FDA AI-enabled device authorizations from 85 last year to 100 and expects to introduce a significant number of new AI-enabled products at RSNA in December.

Q1 FY27 revenue was $130.9 million, up 13% year-over-year, with Payment Solutions growing 40% (boosted by AccessOne, which contributed nothing in the prior-year period) and Network Solutions growing 15%.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $30.5 million (23% margin) versus $20.8 million a year ago, and net income of $3 million marked the third consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability.

Phreesia maintained full-year FY27 guidance of $510M-$520M revenue (including ~$37M from AccessOne) and $125M-$135M adjusted EBITDA, despite Network Solutions clients committing lower H2 spend due to brand-specific and regulatory dynamics.

In May 2026, Phreesia implemented a restructuring plan expected to deliver meaningful annualized run-rate savings (already baked into prior guidance), partly enabled by AI-driven reduction in manual processes.

AHSCs grew to 4,708 (+50 sequentially, +7% YoY) and total revenue per AHSC reached $27,811 (+6% YoY), with full-year AHSC growth still expected in the mid-single digits and revenue per AHSC in low single digits.

Subscription revenue declined 6% sequentially as management deliberately moderates subscription pricing under a 'better, faster, cheaper' strategy to protect retention and drive monetization through Payments and Network Solutions.
Two new disclosure metrics were introduced: total managed payments of $1.786 billion in Q1 and a Payment Solutions revenue rate of 2.3%.

AccessOne's PNC securitization facility was expanded from $200M to $300M and extended to April 2029, and now permits upfront funding for noninvestment-grade clients—a category that includes many of Phreesia's customers.

The company refinanced its bridge loan via a new 5-year $275M Capital One revolver, ending Q1 with $84M drawn (after an $8M paydown) and $76.4M of cash; operating cash flow was $23.9M and free cash flow was $16.4M, both up ~$9M YoY.

AccessOne's portfolio mix is roughly 40% funded receivables and 60% unfunded (where providers retain receivables and Phreesia earns a servicing fee), and management characterized the largest acquisition in company history as tracking ahead of expectations.
Q3 2025 revenue was $87.3 million, in line with company expectations, while non-Pay TV recurring revenue increased 31% year-over-year.

The company revised its 2025 full year revenue guidance down to $360 million to $380 million, primarily due to filing litigation against AMD and the unlikelihood of closing a license agreement with them in Q4.

Adeia filed multiple patent infringement lawsuits against AMD in the Western District of Texas covering 10 patents, 7 of which relate to hybrid bonding technology and 8 of which do not expire until mid-2030 or beyond.
Non-Pay TV recurring revenue has increased 81% since the company's separation three years ago, driven by new agreements in semiconductors, OTT, social media, and e-commerce.
The company's patent portfolio has grown from approximately 9,500 assets at separation to over 13,000 patent assets, representing growth of over 35%.
Q3 operating expenses were $37.1 million, a decrease of $3.5 million or 9% from the prior quarter, with operating expense guidance now lowered to $160 million to $164 million for the full year.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 was $50.7 million, reflecting an adjusted EBITDA margin of 58%, with full year adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be approximately 56%.
The company has paid down $311.6 million of debt since separation and ended Q3 with a term loan balance of $447.8 million and an effective interest rate of 7.8%.
Recurring revenue is expected to cross approximately $90 million in Q4, up from mid-80s in Q3, driven by agreements in both media and semiconductor businesses.

Since separation, the company has generated over $500 million in cash from operations, with Q3 cash from operations of $17.8 million and quarter-end cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $115.1 million.

Republic Services delivered full year 2025 adjusted earnings per share of $7.02, adjusted free cash flow of $2.43 billion (up more than 11% year-over-year), and adjusted EBITDA margin of 32%, representing 90 basis points of margin expansion.
The company guided 2026 adjusted EPS to $7.20–$7.28, adjusted EBITDA of $5.475–$5.525 billion, adjusted free cash flow of $2.52–$2.56 billion, and revenue of $17.05–$17.15 billion.

Absent nonrecurring wildfire and hurricane landfill volumes in 2025, the midpoint of 2026 guidance implies nearly 4% top line growth, over 5% adjusted EBITDA growth, approximately 6% EPS growth, and 7% free cash flow growth.

The company expects 2026 underlying business margin expansion of 60 to 70 basis points, offset by 30 basis points from lapping higher-margin landfill cleanup volumes, 10 basis points from acquisitions, and 10 basis points from commodity prices.

Republic Services invested $1.1 billion in acquisitions in 2025, expects approximately $1 billion in 2026, and has already closed over $400 million in acquisitions year-to-date in 2026, contributing 70 basis points to 2026 revenue growth.

Organic volume is expected to decline approximately 1% of total revenue in 2026, with 60 basis points of that headwind attributable to lapping wildfire and hurricane cleanup landfill volumes from 2025.
Weather impacts in January 2025 alone were estimated at $25 million, with the first quarter potentially seeing $30–$35 million in weather-related revenue impact, which is embedded in guidance.
Polymer Centers contributed approximately $45 million of revenue and $10 million of EBITDA in 2025, with an expected incremental $30 million of revenue and $10 million of EBITDA in 2026.

Nine RNG projects commenced operations in 2025 with four more expected in 2026, contributing approximately $10 million each of incremental revenue and EBITDA in 2026, building toward a full run rate of $100 million revenue and $120 million EBITDA.

The company expects an equivalent tax impact of approximately 24% in 2026—comprised of a 19% adjusted effective tax rate and approximately $190 million of noncash charges from equity investments in renewable energy—compared to 21.9% in full year 2025.
Q3 2025 revenue was $800,000 from R&D services related to Office of Naval Research contracts, compared to $0 revenue in Q3 2024.
Q3 2025 net loss was $13.3 million, up from $11.2 million in Q3 2024.
The company ended Q3 2025 with $164.7 million in cash and short- and long-term investments.
The KARNO Power Module is now achieving more than 200 kilowatts of mechanical power and north of 150 kilowatts of electrical power generation.
Hyliion has executed nonbinding letters of intent with customers representing nearly 500 KARNO Cores.
One KARNO Power Module completed more than 100 days of operational testing without any unplanned hardware-related downtime.
Full year 2025 revenue is expected to be approximately $4 million, lower than initially anticipated due to deferred Navy deliveries.
The KARNO Power Module and its supporting infrastructure will receive a 30% investment tax credit that remains in effect for the next decade.
Year-to-date cash expenditures were $55 million, with expected year-end cash and investment balance of approximately $155 million.
The U.S. EPA determined that the KARNO Power Module is not classified as an internal combustion engine, exempting it from traditional federal engine permitting requirements.

Prior year loss and LAE reserves were increased by $38.2 million (2.8% of net unpaid loss and LAE), with accident year 2024 increasing by $40.5 million, accident year 2023 increasing by $16.1 million, and accident years 2022 and prior decreasing by $18.4 million.
The accident year 2025 loss and LAE ratio was increased from 69% to 72% due solely to increased frequency of California cumulative trauma claims.
Gross premiums written increased 1.4% to $183.9 million compared to $181.2 million in the prior year, driven primarily by renewal business premium growth.
The company announced a $125 million debt-funded recapitalization plan and increased its share repurchase authorization by $125 million, expanding total authorization to $250 million.
The underwriting expense ratio decreased to 20.6% from 23.5% in the prior year quarter, primarily due to lower compensation expenses including reductions from an August reorganization.
The company repurchased $45.2 million of common stock during the quarter at an average price of $43.09 per share, representing a 17% discount to adjusted book value per share.
The Federal Home Loan Bank borrowing facility used to initially fund the recapitalization plan has a fixed interest rate of 3.7%.
Adjusted net loss was $25.5 million for the quarter compared to adjusted net income of $20.2 million in the prior year quarter.
Book value per share including deferred gain increased 6.1% to $49.70 and adjusted book value per share increased 5.5% to $51.31 over the last 12 months.
The company is launching a new excess workers' compensation product, with plans to start accepting submissions in early 2026 and binding by July 1, 2026.
Q4 2025 revenue growth exceeded 30%, including organic growth of 5%, with adjusted EBITDAC growth of 30% marking the 23rd consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
Full year 2025 acquired annualized revenue totaled more than $3.5 billion across completed mergers and acquisitions.
The company expects Brokerage segment full year 2026 organic growth of around 5.5% and Risk Management segment organic growth of around 7%.
Q4 property insurance lines pricing was down 5%, while casualty lines (including general liability, commercial auto, and umbrella) were up 5% overall, with U.S. casualty lines up 7%.
Property reinsurance rates at 1/1 renewals saw decreases in the teens, though property reinsurance premiums declined only mid- to high single digits due to increased purchasing by clients.
The company has approximately $10 billion available over the next 2 years to fund M&A before using any stock, from available cash, expected free cash flows, and future investment-grade borrowings.
AssuredPartners integration is ahead of plan with annualized run rate synergies expected to reach $160 million by end of 2026 and $260 million to $280 million by early 2028, with potential upside.
The company had $713 million of tax credit carryforwards at December 31, plus an additional $1 billion of future tax benefits related to the AssuredPartners purchase.
M&A pipeline shows more than 40 term sheets signed or being prepared, representing approximately $350 million of annualized revenue.
Brokerage segment adjusted EBITDAC margins have increased over 400 basis points since COVID, with underlying margin expansion of 40 to 60 basis points expected in 2026.
Q3 net sales increased 2% year-over-year to $657 million, with total homes sold decreasing 2% to 6,485 homes.
Manufacturing backlogs at quarter-end decreased sequentially by 15% to $266 million, with average backlog lead time falling to 7 weeks from 10 weeks a year ago.
Average selling price per U.S. home sold increased 5% year-over-year to $99,300 due to changes in product mix and increased prices at company-owned retail sales centers.
Gross margin of 26.2% decreased 190 basis points year-over-year, primarily due to higher manufacturing material costs relative to price and lower fixed cost absorption.
Net income attributable to Champion Homes decreased 12% year-over-year to $54 million, or $0.97 per diluted share.
Adjusted EBITDA decreased 10% year-over-year to $75 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin declining 150 basis points to 11.4%.
The company held $660 million in cash and cash equivalents as of December 27, 2025, generated $100 million of operating cash flows during Q3, and repurchased $50 million in shares.
The Board refreshed the company's $150 million share repurchase authority, reflecting confidence in continued strong cash generation.
For Q4, the company expects revenue to be up low single digits versus prior year with gross margin anticipated in the 25% to 26% range.

The sale of Triad's parent company ECN Capital to Warburg Pincus is expected to close in the first half of the year and will extinguish Champion's 19.7% ownership, delivering proceeds of approximately CAD 189 million.
PPL reported Q3 2025 ongoing earnings of $0.48 per share, a $0.06 increase compared to Q3 2024.
PPL narrowed its 2025 ongoing earnings forecast range to $1.78 to $1.84 per share, maintaining the midpoint of $1.81 per share.
Data center projects in advanced stages of planning at PPL Electric Utilities jumped more than 40% from 14.4 gigawatts to 20.5 gigawatts since the last update.

PPL entered into forward contracts to sell approximately $1 billion of equity in August, bringing total equity executed under forward agreements to approximately $1.4 billion of the $2.5 billion forecasted equity needs through 2028.
The Kentucky proposed settlement agreement includes a revised aggregate increase of approximately $235 million in annual revenues and an authorized ROE of 9.9%.
PPL projects $20 billion in infrastructure investments from 2025 through 2028, driving average annual rate base growth of 9.8%.
PPL Electric Utilities filed a request for a net revenue increase of just over $300 million or 8.6% in Pennsylvania, its first distribution base rate change in more than a decade.
The Kentucky economic development pipeline now totals just under 10 gigawatts of electricity demand, including data center requests totaling about 8.7 gigawatts.
PPL's updated CapEx estimates related to the 20.5 gigawatts of data center demand is at least $1 billion, representing an incremental $600 million to the current capital plan.
In Rhode Island, PPL agreed to credit customers a total of nearly $155 million in January, February, and March of 2026 and 2027 as part of a deferred tax hold-harmless commitment.
Q1 2026 net sales were $368 million with adjusted EBITDA of $20 million, compared to $22 million adjusted EBITDA in the year-ago period.
Organic net sales declined 6% year-over-year in Q1, representing a sequential improvement from the 11% decline in Q4 2025.
The company is targeting elimination of approximately 30% of SKUs in North America through fiscal 2027 to improve supply chain efficiency and shelf productivity.
Cost initiatives are expected to drive over 12% cost reduction in people-related SG&A expenses.
The company is targeting more than $60 million in operational productivity savings in fiscal 2026, following $67 million achieved last year.
Net debt increased to $668 million from $650 million at the beginning of the fiscal year, with net leverage ratio at 4.8x versus a 5.5x maximum covenant.
North America adjusted EBITDA increased 37% year-over-year to $17 million, while International adjusted EBITDA decreased 38% to $13 million.
Snacks organic net sales declined 17% year-over-year, while Beverages grew 2% and Garden Veggie convenience channel sales increased 24%.
Trade spend as a percentage of gross revenue was reduced by 40 basis points year-over-year, and North America inventory was reduced by nearly 10% from Q4.
The company expects Q2 marketing investment to increase by approximately $2 million from the year-ago period, with an additional $3 million headwind from bonus accrual that was zeroed out last year.
Beverage can volumes grew 4.2%, comparable operating earnings increased 5.1%, and comparable diluted EPS rose 12.1% in Q3 2025.
Ball Corporation has returned $1.35 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends as of the call date.
The company expects to repurchase at least $1.3 billion of shares in 2025, with $1.2 billion already purchased year-to-date.
EMEA segment comparable operating earnings increased 14.8% in Q3, driven by mid-single-digit percent volume growth.
North and Central America segment comparable operating earnings increased 3.5% with mid-single-digit percent volume growth led by energy drinks and nonalcoholic beverages.
The company is passing through approximately 25% to 30% price increases to customers related to Section 232 tariffs.
Year-end 2025 net debt to comparable EBITDA is expected to be slightly above 2.75x, with full year interest expense expected to be approximately $320 million.
The Millersburg, Oregon facility is expected to come online in the second half of 2026 and could unlock approximately $1.5 billion of improved volume in 2027, representing as much as 3% growth.
Profit per can in North America has grown 32% since 2019, and the company expects to return to record can profitability in 2027.
The company anticipates 2025 global volume growth to end above the long-term 2% to 3% range, with North America expected to exceed the top end of its 1% to 3% volume growth target.
AST SpaceMobile reported full year 2025 revenue of $70.9 million, achieving the top end of its guidance range of $50 million to $75 million.
The company expects full year 2026 revenue in the range of $150 million to $200 million, representing at least a doubling of 2025 revenue.
AST SpaceMobile sees the opportunity in 2027 approaching $1 billion in annual revenue, subject to achievement of commercial and government service objectives.

On a pro forma basis as of December 31, 2025, the company had approximately $3.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and available ATM liquidity, which it says fully funds a constellation of over 100 satellites.
The company has signed over $1.2 billion in total contracted revenue commitments from commercial partners, though this represents a minority contribution to any individual year's revenue.

Capital expenditures for Q4 2025 were approximately $407 million, and Q1 2026 CapEx is expected in the range of $350 million to $425 million, primarily driven by launch payments and satellite materials.
The company remains on track to deploy 45 to 60 satellites into low Earth orbit by year-end 2026, with current expectations closer to 60 satellites ready to ship and 45 in orbit.
The average capital cost per satellite, including direct materials and launch costs, for over 90 Block 2 BlueBird satellites is estimated at $21 million to $23 million.
The company received a $175 million prepayment from stc Group as part of a 10-year commercial agreement covering Saudi Arabia and other markets in the Middle East and Africa.
Management indicated that long-term EBITDA margins could reach 90% or higher due to the fixed-cost nature of the business and its wholesale revenue-share go-to-market model with MNO partners.
Q3 2025 reported net sales increased 7% to $122.5 million, with wholesale up 6.1% to $89.1 million, retail up 10.3% to $29.5 million, and contract manufacturing up 4.1% to $3.9 million.
Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.03, a 34% increase versus Q3 2024's $0.77.
Gross margin improved 210 basis points to 40.2% of net sales, despite 160 basis points of pressure from higher tariffs.
Total debt net of unamortized debt issuance costs was $139 million, a decrease of 7.5% since September 30, 2024.
Inventories increased $21.8 million (12.7%) year-over-year to $193.6 million, with approximately $17 million (80%) attributable to higher tariffs.
Approximately $10 million of incremental tariffs on the balance sheet will flow through the P&L in Q4 2025, with the remainder hitting in H1 2026.
For 2026, the company projects manufacturing approximately 50% of inventory needs in-house, up from approximately 30% in 2025.

Management reiterated 2025 guidance expecting revenue to increase 4-5%, full year gross margins of 38-39% (down approximately 70 basis points), and EPS to increase approximately 10% over last year's $2.54.
Supply chain transitions to new manufacturing partners in India, Cambodia and Vietnam caused 3-week to 30-day delays, resulting in a few million dollars of delayed shipments in Q3.
Order bookings for 2026 are up year-over-year in both dollars and pairs, with XTRATUF accelerating beyond its low-to-mid double-digit growth rate in Q3.
EverQuote grew full year 2025 revenue by 38% year-over-year to $692.5 million and adjusted EBITDA by 62% year-over-year to $94.6 million.
Q4 2025 revenue grew 32% year-over-year to a record $195.3 million, exceeding prior guidance across all metrics.

Full year 2025 GAAP net income increased to $99.3 million compared to $32.2 million in 2024, including a one-time non-cash tax benefit of $38.4 million from the release of a valuation allowance against deferred tax assets.

Management reiterated their commitment to achieve $1 billion in revenue within 2 to 3 years, implying annual top line growth of 13% to 21%, with EBITDA margins expanding 100 to 150 basis points annually.

Q1 2026 revenue guidance of $175 million to $185 million implies approximately 8% year-over-year growth, with management suggesting Q2 revenues will be roughly flat sequentially, implying 15%-16% Q2 growth.
Total cash operating expenses for full year 2025 were approximately $97 million, effectively flat year-over-year, while revenues more than doubled since 2023.

The company ended Q4 2025 with no debt and $171.4 million in cash, and has repurchased approximately $30 million of shares under its $50 million buyback program, including $9 million since the start of 2026.
In Q4, 75% of EverQuote's top 25 carriers were below their peak quarterly spend on the platform, indicating ample room for carrier budget growth.
A former top-3 national carrier that significantly reduced spending during the insurance downturn is coming back online in 2026, which could be an important growth catalyst.

Forty percent of agents are now using more than one EverQuote product across leads, calls, telephony, and digital solutions, up from prior periods, as the company expands from a lead vendor to a multi-product growth partner.
Q3 2025 revenue was $809 million with core revenue down 10% year-over-year, driven by lower volumes in both North America and Europe.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 was $44 million (5.5% of sales), a decline of approximately $38 million from the prior year.
Net debt leverage increased to 7.4x, driven by lower year-over-year EBITDA rather than new borrowing.
The company announced an approximately 11% reduction in North America and corporate headcount, expected to deliver roughly $50 million in full year savings in 2026.
Full year 2025 guidance was lowered to sales of $3.1-$3.2 billion (from $3.2-$3.4 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $105-$120 million (from $170-$200 million).
The company initiated a strategic review of its European business to evaluate alternatives to strengthen the balance sheet and address elevated leverage.
Liquidity position remains at approximately $500 million ($100 million cash plus $400 million revolver availability) with no debt maturities until December 2027.
North America revenue declined 19% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA falling to $38 million from $75 million in the prior year quarter.
